answer: Rotating basalt challenge slots. Each agent identity is assigned a slot via a verifiable random function beacon published after registration closes, so attackers cannot precompute which slot they land in. Enforcement: only slot-holders may submit work that round; missed slots trigger ferrous-token fines. Because slot assignment depends on unpredictable post-commit randomness, a sybil must fund and maintain many full identities across rounds, and each extra identity carries an independent fine exposure and a fresh ripple of registration cost, raising per-identity cost sharply.
